beats.narration_en: Same emergency stop. Only one of these cars can still steer.
Slam the brakes without ABS and the wheels lock.
A locked tire stops rolling and starts to slide
and a sliding tire can't push the car sideways.
So turn the wheel all you want and the car still goes straight.
ABS stops the wheels from locking.
Behind each wheel a sensor counts the teeth on a spinning ring
so the computer knows how fast every wheel is turning.
When one wheel slows down faster than the car it's about to lock
so ABS eases the brake on that wheel for an instant and squeezes again
The tire keeps rolling at the edge of its grip so it can still steer.
That buzz in the pedal is ABS working. Keep pressing and steer.
